title: Summit Welcome Email
task: A welcome email for new members of Summit Climbing Gym
intro: Five choices shape the email. Each option shows the result, so you can pick what you see.

questions.label: Tone
questions.question: What tone suits the welcome email?
questions.evidence: You said this is a climbing gym.

options.label: Stoked
options.text: A stoked voice sounds like climbers talk to each other and fits a gym, but it can read as try-hard to a quiet member.

preview.title: You're in. Let's send it.
body: Welcome to the crew! Chalk up, grab a pair of shoes, and come play on the wall.
Your first climb is on us.

options.label: Warm
options.text: A warm voice is friendly and personal and suits a mixed membership, but it has less energy.

preview.title: Welcome to Summit
body: We are glad that you joined us. Take your time, ask anyone for help, and enjoy your first visit.

options.label: Plain
options.text: A plain voice gives the facts first and reads fastest, but it can feel like a receipt.

preview.title: Your membership is active
body: Your membership is active from today. The gym is open 6am to 10pm every day.
Bring a towel and a water bottle.

options.label: Hero and cards
options.text: A big photo opens the email, then three cards lead to the next steps, but it needs good photos.

options.label: One column
options.text: Short text runs down one column to a single button, which is simple, but it shows no photos.

options.label: Photo beside text
options.text: A photo sits beside the welcome text, so the email feels personal, but it breaks on narrow phones.

preview.caption: Photo and text side by side

options.label: Chalk and flame
options.text: A light page with a hot orange button looks lively in a bright gym, but orange on white is hard to read at small sizes.

options.label: Granite night
options.text: A dark page with a green accent feels bold and modern, but some mail apps change dark colours.

options.label: Sky and rope
options.text: Soft blues feel calm and clear on every screen, but the email looks like many other emails.

questions.label: Booking
questions.question: How do new members book their first class?

options.label: Pick a day
options.text: The member picks a day inside the email, which is the fastest path, but many mail apps block this.

preview.alt: A row of day buttons. Clicking a day books the class.
preview.html:
Book your intro class

Pick a day.
preview.js: var b=document.querySelectorAll('.days button'),m=document.getElementById('m');b.forEach(function(x){x.onclick=function(){b.forEach(function(y){y.className=''});x.className='on';m.textContent='Booked for '+x.textContent+' at 6pm. See you at the wall.'}})

options.label: One button
options.text: One button opens a short booking page, so every mail app works, but the member leaves the email.

preview.alt: A single button. Clicking it shows the booking page that opens next.
preview.js: document.getElementById('go').onclick=function(){var m=document.getElementById('m');m.textContent='Booking page opens: choose a day and a time.';m.className='show'}

options.label: Reply to book
options.text: The member replies to the email and staff book the class, which feels personal, but it adds staff work.

questions.label: Extras
questions.question: Which extras does the email need?

options.label: Opening hours
options.text: Members see when to come, and the hours rarely change, but hours add length.

preview.alt: A small table of opening hours.

options.label: Map
options.text: A map helps a first visit, but it needs a picture file that some mail apps block.

preview.alt: A simple map with streets and a pin on the gym.

options.label: Class timetable
options.text: The week shows which classes suit a beginner, but the timetable changes often.

options.label: Gear prices
options.text: Members know the cost of hire before they arrive, but the prices go out of date.
